# Open-source AI job-search tools on GitHub — research findings (Sept 2026)

Reader lens throughout: a 45–60-year-old, non-technical, mid-career job seeker (unemployed or unhappy at work). "Usability verdict" = could this reader realistically use it this weekend? "Collegica angle" = could Collegica build a small, local, browser-tab tool from it (the site's house style — see the `budget-from-statements` article precedent)?

Star counts are approximate as of 2026-09-10. All repos public.

---

## 0. The landscape in one paragraph

Three big shifts since 2024:

1. **The center of gravity moved from "bots that apply for you" to "AI that prepares, you submit."** The two most-starred projects in the space — `career-ops` (71k) and `MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search` (42k) — both *explicitly refuse* to auto-submit. Even `job-ops` says outright: "Recruiters can tell when applications are automated." AIHawk, the 2024 poster child for LinkedIn auto-apply, quietly pivoted into a generic browser-automation agent.
2. **"Runs inside your AI coding CLI" is the new distribution model.** career-ops, ai-job-search, interview-skills, ats-resume-agent, job-hunt-copilot etc. are not apps — they're prompt/skill packages you drop into Claude Code / Codex / OpenCode. Powerful, cheap, but assumes a terminal. That's a real accessibility gap for our reader, and an opening.
3. **Platforms are fighting back.** LinkedIn's March 2026 transparency report: 23.5M automated sessions flagged in one quarter. Indeed/Glassdoor now speed-profile submissions (~30–50/day thresholds reported), hidden CAPTCHAs, and down-rank on resume/profile inconsistencies. Auto-apply is now a genuine account-risk for someone whose LinkedIn is their professional identity of 25 years — which is exactly our reader.

Low stars, keyword-stuffed topics. Treat as noise. |

**Usability verdict for our reader:** *Do not recommend.* Every one needs Python + a driven Chrome, and every one exposes the reader's real LinkedIn account to restriction. The people these bots suit (new grads firing 300 applications) are the opposite of a 52-year-old whose value is a specific track record and a network. Volume is not their problem; targeting is.

**ToS/ban reality:** LinkedIn User Agreement bans "automated software … to access, scrape, crawl" the service; the 2024 clarification allows extensions that *assist the user's own reviewed actions*. Auto-submitters without review are the gray-to-red zone. Indeed/Glassdoor reportedly speed-profile and down-rank. GodsScion's disclaimer puts compliance on the user. AIHawk's own issues show accounts hitting Easy Apply limits.

**Collegica angle:** the *dry-run* and *screening-question memory* features are the good ideas here — an assistant that drafts your answers to the standard screening questions once, so you paste them, is useful and ToS-safe.

| [NullSpace-BitCradle/ats-resume-agent](https://github.com/NullSpace-BitCradle/ats-resume-agent) | 9 | Yes | — | Claude Code agent: tailor to JD with **"zero fabrication — every claim sourced from your career document"**, LaTeX PDF | TeX + Claude Code |
| [vmlgtm/imprintcv](https://github.com/vmlgtm/imprintcv) | 1 | New | — | Same anti-hallucination idea done deterministically: "zero-token fact verification" so the LLM can't alter your metrics; Typst-in-WASM PDF | TypeScript |

The right substrate for "one master file, many tailored outputs". | JS |
| [sliday/resume-job-matcher](https://github.com/sliday/resume-job-matcher) | 269 | Yes | — | The *other side*: recruiter-side AI screening CLI. Useful for showing readers how they're scored ("every score cites the resume span behind it"). | TypeScript |

**Usability verdict:** **Reactive Resume (hosted) and OpenResume's ATS-parser test are usable today by anyone with a browser** — the only two in the whole survey that clear that bar with zero install. Resume-Matcher is the best *capability* but needs Docker. JadeAI is close (hosted demo, but keys in browser is a trust ask).

**Collegica angle:** This is the strongest category for a Collegica browser-tab tool. The recurring, valuable, *safe* pattern is: master résumé (JSON Resume) + job description → (a) what the ATS actually reads, (b) keyword gap, (c) a tailored draft **with a fabrication guard** (ats-resume-agent / imprintcv idea). All of it can run client-side with a BYO key or a local model. Nothing touches LinkedIn.

| [DaKheera47/job-ops](https://github.com/DaKheera47/job-ops) | 3.9k | Yes | AGPL-3.0 + Commons Clause | "DevOps for job hunting": scrapes 10+ boards, AI fit-score, tailored CV, Gmail-based status tracking. Explicitly **no auto-apply**. | TypeScript/Next.js, Docker |
| [pinloop-ai/pinloop-cli](https://github.com/pinloop-ai/pinloop-cli) | 329 | New (Aug 2026) | MIT (CLI only) | 10k+ postings from 4k employers refreshed hourly, judged against your profile — but backend is a **freemium hosted service**. | Node |
| [PaulMcInnis/JobFunnel](https://github.com/PaulMcInnis/JobFunnel) | 2.2k | **Archived** | MIT | The 2017–2022 classic: scrape into one deduped spreadsheet. Dead; listed for history. | Python |
| [kitsuno-ai/agentic-job-search-eu](https://github.com/kitsuno-ai/agentic-job-search-eu) | 5 | Yes | — | Machine-readable directory of EU job sources with access type / rate limits. Small but the *idea* (a curated source list) is exactly what a reader needs. | YAML |
| [crchalfant/Job-Search-Autopilot](https://github.com/crchalfant/Job-Search-Autopilot) | 5 | Yes | — | Searches 13 sources daily, Claude rates, emails a ranked morning digest, Kanban board. "Built so anyone can make it their own by telling an AI what they want." | Python/Flask |

**Usability verdict:** freehire.me (hosted) is the only one a non-technical reader can use as-is — and it's arguably the most interesting one, because it *bypasses* LinkedIn/Indeed and goes straight to employer ATS pages (which is where the 45+ hidden-market roles actually live). Everything else is developer tooling.

**Collegica angle:** The "morning digest" pattern (Job-Search-Autopilot) — a small script that pulls a curated set of employer ATS feeds and has an LLM rank them against your one-page profile — is a very Collegica-shaped tool, and it's ToS-clean if it reads Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby public JSON feeds rather than scraping LinkedIn.

**Usability verdict:** Nothing here is turnkey for a non-engineer, and almost all of it is tuned for Big-Tech coding interviews. That is the gap: **behavioural / experience-based interviewing for experienced people** — "tell me about a time you led…", handling "aren't you overqualified?", age-adjacent questions — is what our reader needs and none of these target it.

**Collegica angle:** interview-skills' *structure* (JD + résumé → questions + follow-ups + answer guidance) is trivially reproducible as a prompt the reader pastes into any chat model. A Collegica article can give the prompt directly; no tool needed.

Creator: 69 tailored applications → hired. | Claude Code, Python 3.10, Bun, LaTeX |

| [6figr-com/jobgpt-mcp-server](https://github.com/6figr-com/jobgpt-mcp-server) | 22 | Yes | — | MCP server exposing a hosted JobGPT service (search, auto-apply, résumé) to Claude/Cursor — hosted backend, not fully open | TypeScript |

**Usability verdict:** career-ops is the single most important project in this survey — 71k stars in five months, MIT, refuses to spam, and its A–H evaluation rubric is *exactly* the kind of disciplined method Collegica writes about. But the honest verdict for a 55-year-old operations manager: "install Node, pick an AI CLI, work in a terminal" is a wall. Maybe 1 in 20 readers will do it. The *method* (structured evaluation before applying; fit score; rejection-pattern review) transfers to anyone with ChatGPT/Claude in a browser.

**Collegica angle:** Translate career-ops' A–H rubric into a plain prompt + a Markdown "job evaluation" template the reader keeps in a folder — mirroring the aging-well article's "plans as documents, under version control, reviewed quarterly" habit. That is the article.

The closest thing to a "download and double-click" local tool. |
| [vinaygiri/hiresignal-personal](https://github.com/vinaygiri/hiresignal-personal) | 3 | Yes | — | Local semantic matching (sqlite-vec + Ollama), company due-diligence |

**Usability verdict:** The privacy argument matters enormously for this audience (they are pasting 25 years of salary history and employer names into something). Ollama-capable tools exist, but every one needs Docker or a dev toolchain. ai-job-hunter-app's desktop-binary approach is the right *form factor* and worth watching.

**Collegica angle:** Reuse the "plan in ratios, not identifiers" rule from the aging-well article: an anonymized master résumé (`[Employer_A]`, "$X"-style) that's safe to paste anywhere. That's a technique, not a tool, and it's cheaper than Ollama.

## 7. Things to warn readers about

- **README-only "open source" that's a paid product:** `lookr-fyi/job-application-bot-by-ollama-ai` (467 stars, no code, no license, sells JobHuntr at $9.99+). Also `jobgpt-mcp-server` and `pinloop-cli` are thin clients for hosted freemium backends (legit, but not "free and local").
- **SEO-farm repos:** anything titled "Best LinkedIn Auto Apply Bot (2026)" with 2–60 stars and 20 topics.
- **Abandoned:** JobFunnel (archived), open-resume (no commits since Oct 2024 — hosted site still works), jsonresume/resume-cli & resume-schema (archived → moved to monorepo, still fine to use), darsan-in/Job-Hunter (archived).
- **AGPL / Commons Clause** on ApplyPilot, open-resume, offerPilot, job-ops — irrelevant to a reader, relevant if Collegica ever forks code into a hosted tool.
- **Name collisions:** three unrelated "ApplyPilot"s; two "career-ops"; several "ai-job-search"es. Link by URL, not name.
- **Fabrication risk** is the quiet one: most tailoring tools will happily invent a metric. Only ats-resume-agent and imprintcv make "no fabrication" a design constraint. A reader with a 25-year record has the most to lose from an invented bullet in a background check.

---

## Top 5 worth a reader's time (non-technical, 45–60)

1. **Reactive Resume — rxresu.me** (42k, MIT). Free, hosted, no account, privacy-first, exports PDF/DOCX/JSON. The one tool to *actually use* this weekend.
2. **OpenResume's ATS parser test — open-resume.com** (8.9k, AGPL, stale but hosted). Upload the PDF you've been sending; see what the machine reads. The single most eye-opening 60 seconds for someone with a 2008-era two-column résumé.
3. **freehire.me** (653, MIT, hosted). Search 3.3M postings pulled straight from employer career pages / 92 ATSs — the "hidden" postings that never get boosted on LinkedIn, and no automation on your own account.
4. **career-ops** (71k, MIT) — *as a method, not an install.* Its A–H evaluation rubric and 1–5 fit score, its refusal to spam, and its "analyze rejection patterns" step are the discipline to teach. We can hand readers the rubric as a prompt.
5. **Resume-Matcher** (28k, Apache-2.0) — for the 1-in-10 reader (or their adult kid) willing to run one Docker command: local Ollama option, keyword gap, tailored draft, cover letter, interview prep, all on your own machine.

Honourable mention for the tool-builder in the house: **JSON Resume** as the master-file format, **Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby public feeds** as the ToS-clean job source, and **imprintcv / ats-resume-agent** for the fabrication guard. Those three are the skeleton of a Collegica "small local tool that runs in a browser tab."
